Monday, November 16, 2026

Daily Brief

The day's most consequential developments center on escalating conflicts and diplomatic standoffs. In Yemen, government forces have withdrawn from strategic positions near the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the interim capital Aden from advancing Houthi fighters, a move that could reshape the war's trajectory [BBC, Al Jazeera]. Iran announced it will block IAEA inspectors from accessing its damaged nuclear facilities until US conditions are met, following last year's strikes that killed Supreme Leader Khamenei [France 24]. Ukraine launched its largest drone barrage of the war—over 1,300 drones—striking targets including a key Crimea bridge, while Russia claimed to intercept most of them [Le Monde, Globe and Mail]. In Europe, five EU nations are expected to announce a pilot migrant deportation center in Rwanda, testing a new approach to asylum policy [BBC]. At COP31 in Turkey, Australia released a draft deal calling for 'accelerated action' to phase out fossil fuels, though significant gaps remain among negotiating parties [The Hindu, RFI]. Meanwhile, attention turns to this week's Trump-Xi meeting at the APEC summit, though analysts suggest substantive breakthroughs on trade or security are unlikely [Globe and Mail, Nikkei Asia].

Top Stories
01 Conflict

Yemen Government Forces Withdraw from Bab al-Mandab to Defend Aden from Houthi Advance

  • Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces announced withdrawal from Dhubab Airport and territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait to reinforce positions around Aden, Yemen's interim capital
  • Houthi forces have claimed control of evacuated territory, including areas seized in a September offensive such as Perim Island and the port city of Mokha
  • Fighting now centers on a strategic triangle linking Aden, the besieged city of Taiz, and the Bab al-Mandab maritime chokepoint connecting the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden
  • Military analysts describe this triangle as the 'strategic centre of gravity' that could determine the war's outcome

02 Geopolitics

Iran Blocks UN Nuclear Inspectors Until US Meets Conditions for Ending Middle East War

  • Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi announced Iran will deny IAEA access to damaged nuclear facilities until Iranian conditions are met and the war has 'permanently ended'
  • Nuclear site inspections have been suspended since last year's 12-day war with Israel, during which US strikes also hit Iranian nuclear facilities
  • IAEA inspectors visited Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant in September but have been denied access to bombed sites including Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan
  • The statement follows IAEA calls for Tehran to resume inspections; Iranian facilities were hit again during the February 2026 war that killed Supreme Leader Khamenei

03 Conflict

Ukraine Launches Record 1,300-Drone Barrage, Strikes Key Crimea Bridge

  • Russia's Defence Ministry claimed to intercept 1,336 Ukrainian drones, the highest number since the 2022 invasion began
  • Ukrainian forces struck a key bridge in Crimea and hit oil depots in Russia's Rostov region, working with pro-Kyiv insurgents inside Russia
  • Six people were wounded in Russia's Krasnodar region and three in Azov city; approximately 600 drones targeted the Moscow region
  • EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas accused Putin of making 'maximalist demands' to extend the conflict as US-mediated talks remain stalled

04 Policy

Five EU Nations to Announce Migrant Deportation Center in Rwanda

  • Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece, and the Netherlands are expected to announce creation of a migrant deportation hub in Rwanda on Monday in Vienna
  • Unlike the scrapped UK scheme, this would apply only to asylum seekers who have exhausted legal avenues to remain in the EU
  • The pilot program would initially host approximately 100 people, with each country potentially sending about 20 migrants
  • Human rights bodies warn the plan could violate migrant rights, though the five countries insist it complies with EU and international law

05 Climate

COP31 Draft Deal Calls for Accelerated Fossil Fuel Phaseout Amid Finance Disputes

  • Australia released first draft of COP31 political agreement calling for 'accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels' in energy systems
  • Draft expresses 'deep concern' over impending breach of Paris Agreement's 1.5°C target and affirms IPCC science
  • Text calls for tripling climate adaptation finance for developing countries to at least $120 billion annually
  • Significant gaps remain among nearly 200 nations with consensus deal due by Friday; summit closes November 20 in Antalya, Turkey
